html:
The Nonuya are a small Witotoan people of the Colombian Amazon, now living mainly on the Caquetá River near Peña Roja, in southern Colombia.

During the Amazon rubber boom the Peruvian Amazon Company of Julio César Arana enslaved the peoples of the Putumayo and Caquetá, and killings and disease nearly destroyed the Nonuya. Survivors married into the Andoke and Muinane, and their own language died out: its last native speaker drowned in 2003. The community has since been working to revive it from recordings and word lists. Their neighbours include the Bora.
sum: The Nonuya are a small Witotoan people of the Colombian Amazon, now living mainly on the Caquetá River near Peña Roja, in southern Colombia.
